# Latin Link: full plain-text summary

Website: https://latinlinkmedical.com/  |  Main site: https://www.latinlink.com  |  LinkedIn: https://uk.linkedin.com/company/latin-link

## Who we are
Latin Link is a specialist translation company founded by a group of linguists and scientists, and a trading name of Language Partners Ltd, 12 Hammersmith Grove, London W6 7AP, United Kingdom. It translates medical, pharmaceutical, life-science, scientific and technical content, with teams across Europe and Latin America. Languages include Spanish for Spain and Latin America, Brazilian and European Portuguese, French, Italian, German, Polish, Dutch, Swedish and translation into English. Every project is translated by a native specialist and reviewed by a second linguist, in a workflow aligned with ISO 17100.

Latin Link has worked closely with the clinical and pharmaceutical industry for 15 years. It is based in London, with production teams across Europe and Latin America working in several time zones. Founded on its expertise in Latin America, it now translates into all major European languages. It focuses on the language pairs it does best rather than claiming every language.

## What makes Latin Link different
- Established, hand-picked team: Every translator is selected for their language pair and subject, and we value and keep a trusted, reliable translator base.
- Perfected through experience: Linguists with at least five years’ translation experience and real work experience in a pharmaceutical, clinical or scientific environment.
- Only into their knowledge area: Specialists translate only within their field and only into their native language, so the science is understood, not just the words.
- No-nonsense about deadlines: A reliable attitude to deadlines, with teams across several time zones and same-day jobs available.

## Services
### Clinical trial translation
URL: https://latinlinkmedical.com/clinical-trial-translation/
Clinical trial translation is the translation of the documents used to plan, run and report a clinical study, such as protocols, informed consent forms, Investigator’s Brochures, patient questionnaires and clinical study reports, so that sponsors, sites, ethics committees and patients in each country receive an exact, consistent version in their own language. At Latin Link, every clinical document is translated by a native specialist and then reviewed by a second linguist.
We use expert translation teams for clinical trial documentation: native linguists with formal scientific qualifications and work experience in a pharmaceutical or clinical environment, who understand the strict deadlines of clinical trials.
Clinical development: Clinical study protocols, synopses and amendments; Investigator’s Brochures (IBs); Informed consent forms and patient information sheets; Clinical study reports (CSRs); Case report forms (CRFs); Ethics committee and site correspondence.
Patient-facing: Patient recruitment documentation; Quality of Life (QoL) instruments and clinical outcome assessments (COAs); Patient information and education materials.

### Regulatory & Latin American submission translation
URL: https://latinlinkmedical.com/regulatory-translation-latin-america/
Regulatory translation for Latin America is the translation of the dossiers, labelling, package inserts and safety documents that health authorities such as ANVISA (Brazil), COFEPRIS (Mexico), INVIMA (Colombia), DIGEMID (Peru) and ANMAT (Argentina) review, into Brazilian Portuguese or the Spanish used in each country. Latin Link was founded on its expertise in Latin America and localises regulatory content for each market.
We translate regulatory, labelling and safety documentation for sponsors and regulatory consultancies, including submissions to health authorities across Latin America.
Regulatory & CMC: Regulatory dossier modules, including CMC/quality; Summaries of Product Characteristics (SmPCs); Patient Information Leaflets (PILs); Drug package inserts and labelling; Safety Data Sheets (SDS); Documents for Latin American submissions.
Safety & pharmacovigilance: Pharmacovigilance documents; Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs); Adverse event reports and case narratives; Hospital and insurance reports.

### Medical device translation
URL: https://latinlinkmedical.com/medical-device-translation/
Medical device translation is the translation and localisation of everything that ships with or supports a device, including instructions for use (IFUs), directions for use (DFUs), labels, packaging, user manuals and safety information, so that users and regulators in each market get exact, consistent and print-ready text.
From initial product labelling and instruction manuals to scientific evaluation and production-ready communications, we help medical device companies achieve their localisation goals.
Medical devices: Instructions for use (IFUs) and directions for use (DFUs); Product labelling and packaging text; Instruction and user manuals; Safety information; Scientific evaluation documents; Production-ready communications.

### Publications & medical communications translation
URL: https://latinlinkmedical.com/medical-communications-translation/
Medical communications translation covers the scientific and educational content written about medicines and medical science, including journal manuscripts and abstracts, medical education, medical brochures and presentations. Much of it is translated into English for publication, where the text must read as if it had been written by a native scientific author.
English is the scientific language of the world. We translate your paper, help optimise it for the guidelines of UK journals, and translate medical education and communications for medical affairs teams and publishers.
Publications & medical communications: Journal submissions, manuscripts and abstracts; Good Medical Practice content for The BMJ, monthly; Medical education and medical brochures; PowerPoint communications and presentations; Research reports; Healthcare websites and marketing materials.

### Machine translation post-editing (MTPE)
A CAT tool machine-translates the document using a translation memory; a specialist translator then checks and edits every line, and editors check it again. Suited to large documents with tight deadlines.

## Sectors
- Medical: Study protocols, ICFs, IBs, SmPCs, PILs, drug package inserts, DFUs, PSURs and hospital and insurance reports.
- Life science: Pharmaceutical and medical device content, from clinical trials and patient recruitment to Quality of Life instruments and device labelling.
- Scientific: Journal manuscripts, research reports and Safety Data Sheets, by translators with a master’s degree or PhD in a scientific discipline.
- Technical: Technical manuals for aerospace, automotive, engineering, energy, IT and telecoms, drawing on our scientific rigour.
Therapy and specialist areas: Audiology, Biotechnology, Cardiology, Cardiovascular, Dermatology, Diagnostics, Endoscopy, General medicine, Gynaecology, Mental health, Neurology, Oncology, Orthopaedics, Pain management, Pharmacology, Urology, Vascular, Women’s health.

## Languages
- Spanish: Traditional Spanish for Spain, and Spanish localised for the 20 Spanish-speaking countries of Latin America.
- Portuguese: Brazilian Portuguese, plus European Portuguese for Portugal and Lusophone Africa, with capacity to scale.
- French & Italian: French for Europe, North America and beyond, and Italian, by native scientific linguists.
- European languages: German, Polish, Dutch, Swedish and other European combinations, managed by our multilingual PMs.
- Into English: Our most requested language: more than 12 million English words translated each year.
- Regional localisation: Local and regional dialects and terminology, localised for the market you are entering.

## Latin American regulators covered
- ANVISA (Brazil): Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária
- COFEPRIS (Mexico): Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios
- INVIMA (Colombia): Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos
- DIGEMID (Peru): Dirección General de Medicamentos, Insumos y Drogas
- ANMAT (Argentina): Administración Nacional de Medicamentos, Alimentos y Tecnología Médica

## Translation process
1. Free, customised quote: Send your files through our client portal or by email. We reply with a fast quote built around your requirements, for one-off projects and long-term partnerships alike.
2. Dedicated account manager: Once confirmed, a dedicated tri-lingual account manager is your point of contact, and the project is delegated to the right linguist for the language and subject.
3. Native specialist translation: A native linguist who works only within their field translates into their mother tongue, using CAT tools, translation memories and your glossaries.
4. Independent review and QA: A second linguist reviews the translation against the source, followed by scientific, statistical, editorial and quality control checks.
5. Delivery on the agreed deadline: Your project manager returns the translation in your required format, on the deadline we agreed.

## Quality
- Two linguists on every project: a native specialist translator and a second reviewing linguist.
- Workflow aligned with ISO 17100 (the international standard for translation services).
- Translation memories and glossaries in Trados and memoQ; desktop publishing for print-ready files.
- Confidential handling; happy to work under the client’s NDA. Client portal for sending files and paying for projects.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is medical translation?
A: Medical translation is the translation of clinical, regulatory, pharmaceutical, medical device and healthcare documents by linguists who understand the science behind them. Errors can affect patients, approvals and trial results, so Latin Link uses native specialists with scientific qualifications and a second reviewing linguist on every project.

Q: What is clinical trial translation?
A: Clinical trial translation is the translation of study documents such as protocols, informed consent forms, Investigator’s Brochures, Quality of Life instruments and clinical study reports, so that sponsors, sites, ethics committees and patients in each country receive an exact, consistent version in their own language.

Q: Which Latin American regulators do you translate documentation for?
A: We translate documentation for submissions to ANVISA (Brazil), COFEPRIS (Mexico), INVIMA (Colombia), DIGEMID (Peru) and ANMAT (Argentina), in Brazilian Portuguese and the Spanish used in each country.

Q: Which languages do you translate?
A: We focus on the language pairs we do best: Spanish (Spain and Latin America), Brazilian and European Portuguese, French, Italian, German, Polish, Dutch, Swedish and other European combinations, plus translation into English. Our translators work only into their native language.

Q: Who are your translators?
A: Native specialists with at least five years’ translation experience and significant work experience in a pharmaceutical or clinical environment. We require qualifications in linguistics and in a scientific discipline; our scientific translators hold a master’s degree or PhD. They translate only within their knowledge area.

Q: Do two linguists really work on every project?
A: Yes. Every project is translated by a native specialist and then reviewed by a second qualified linguist, followed by scientific, statistical, editorial and quality control checks before delivery. It is our standard service, not an add-on.

Q: How does your process relate to ISO 17100?
A: ISO 17100 is the international standard for translation services. Our workflow is aligned with ISO 17100: qualified linguists, revision by a second linguist, managed projects and verification before delivery.

Q: Do you offer machine translation post-editing (MTPE)?
A: Yes. In MTPE a CAT tool first machine-translates the document using a translation memory, then a specialist translator checks and edits every line, and our editors check it again. It suits large documents with tight deadlines.

Q: Can you localise Spanish for different countries?
A: Yes. Our native linguists translate into Spanish for Spain and localise for specific Latin American countries, taking account of each country’s idioms and terminology.

Q: Can you handle urgent or high-volume work?
A: Yes. Same-day jobs are available, and our teams across several time zones let us scale for large, multi-language projects. Tell us your deadline when you request a quote.

Q: Which tools and file formats do you work with?
A: We are experts in Trados and memoQ and use translation memories and glossaries for consistent terminology. We adapt to your preferred CAT tool and have desktop publishing software for print-ready files.

Q: How do you keep our documents confidential?
A: Client documents are shared only with the team working on your project. We are happy to work under your NDA.

Q: How do I get a quote?
A: Use the quote form, email the Latin Link Projects Team or send files through our client portal. We provide free, fast, customised quotes for one-off projects and longer-term partnerships alike.

## Insights
- Translation pitfalls in Latin American clinical trial and regulatory submissions: https://latinlinkmedical.com/insights/latam-clinical-trial-regulatory-translation-pitfalls/
Most delays we see on Latin American submissions are not about the science. They come from treating Spanish or Portuguese as a single language, letting terminology drift across the trial package, or sending patient-facing text that an ethics committee cannot accept.
Newsletter sign-up (mailto, no tracking): https://latinlinkmedical.com/insights/#newsletter
